claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a pre-engineered hierarchical heterostructure.
The hierarchical heterostructure contains designed precipitate phases.
The hierarchical heterostructure contains engineered interphase boundaries.
Quantitative precipitate size, density, and distribution descriptors can be integrated into mechanical-property simulations.
Grain-boundary and interphase-boundary descriptors can be integrated into mechanical-property simulations.
Engineered precipitates and interphase boundaries mediate local stress distributions in HfNbTiVAl10.
Representing the hierarchical features captures localized mechanical responses.
Capturing localized responses provides a better representation of inhomogeneous stress fields.
Better representation of inhomogeneous stress fields improves agreement between predicted and measured Young's modulus.
Better representation of inhomogeneous stress fields improves agreement between predicted and measured yield strength.
Better representation of inhomogeneous stress fields improves agreement between predicted and measured fracture properties.
Under room-temperature, quasi-static tensile and fracture testing, the microstructure-informed model will predict elastic, yield, and fracture properties with 10–15% error relative to experiment.
The microstructure-informed model will reduce simulation run time by approximately 20–30% relative to established methods lacking hierarchical detail.
Conventional simulations omitting hierarchical microstructural descriptors typically have prediction errors exceeding 20%.
Conventional simulations omitting hierarchical microstructural descriptors require longer computation times than the proposed model.
The proposed predictive advantage may fail when high-rate deformation effects dominate the mechanical response.
The proposed predictive advantage may fail when temperature-driven phase transformations dominate the mechanical response.
The proposed predictive advantage may fail when non-hierarchical defects dominate the mechanical response.
The proposed predictive advantage may fail if the hierarchical features are characterized inaccurately.
